Name: Rebirth Brass Band
Notes: Founded 1983 in the Treme by Philip Frazier. The defining contemporary brass band — fuses traditional second line with funk, R&B, and hip-hop. Tuesday night Maple Leaf residency is legendary.

Name: Tuba Skinny
Notes: Traditional New Orleans jazz band led by Shaye Cohn (cornet). Frenchmen Street institution, particularly at d.b.a. Known for their authentic early jazz and blues sound. Large international following.

Name: Soul Rebels
Notes: Brass band that blends second line with hip-hop, funk, and electronic influences. Regular Thursday night residency at Le Bon Temps Roulé. Strong festival circuit presence.

Name: Charmaine Neville
Notes: Daughter of Charles Neville (Neville Brothers). R&B and soul vocalist. Regular Snug Harbor performer. Part of the extended Neville family musical dynasty.

Name: Hot 8 Brass Band
Notes: Grammy-winning brass band from Central City. Known for funk and hip-hop-inflected sound. Regular Howlin' Wolf residency. Survived tragedy and loss to become one of NOLA's most celebrated bands.

Name: Preservation Hall Jazz Band
Notes: Resident band of Preservation Hall, St. Peter St. in the French Quarter. Multiple daily shows year-round. Jazz Fest institution. Preserves and evolves the New Orleans jazz tradition.

Name: George Porter Jr.
Notes: Bassist and co-founder of The Meters, one of the most influential funk bands in history. Regular Daze Between and Jazz Fest performer. Leads his own group and collaborates widely.

Name: Stanton Moore
Notes: Drummer and co-founder of Galactic. Known for deep pocket New Orleans funk drumming. Regular clinician, session musician, and bandleader. Hosts annual Zildjian Jam at Tipitina's.

Name: Dirty Dozen Brass Band
Notes: Founded 1977 in the Treme. One of the originators of the modern brass band movement. Roger Lewis (baritone sax) inducted into Tipitina's Walk of Fame 2026.

Name: Big Freedia
Notes: Queen of Bounce. New Orleans-born LGBTQ+ icon and bounce music pioneer. Regular Jazz Fest and festival presence. Based in the 9th Ward.

Name: Dumpstaphunk
Notes: New Orleans funk supergroup featuring Ivan Neville, Tony Hall, Nick Daniels, and Raymond Weber. Ivan Neville is son of Aaron Neville. Regular Jazz Fest and Daze Between presence.

Name: Trombone Shorty
Notes: Born Troy Andrews in the Treme. Founder of Trombone Shorty Foundation. Leads Orleans Avenue. Annual Shorty Fest fundraiser at Tipitina's. Jazz Fest perennial headliner.

Name: Kermit Ruffins
Notes: Trumpeter, vocalist, and NOLA ambassador. Co-founder of Rebirth Brass Band. Known for BBQ cookouts before shows. Regular presence at Vaughan's Lounge (Thursdays) and multiple festivals.
